What you are running

Orcacode connects a model to a small set of workspace-aware tools: files, shell commands, persistent compute, background processes, task tracking, optional web access, skills, subagents, and MCP servers. The model proposes calls; the host applies policy, approvals, limits, cancellation, and session recording.

THE BOUNDARY

Orcacode is a terminal host, not a hosted control plane. It runs in your workspace and acts with the permissions of the process you started. Treat approval prompts as the last confirmation before a local action.

The quick path

01

Start in the project

Open a terminal in the repository or directory you want the agent to use. The current directory becomes the default workspace root.

02

Ask for a bounded outcome

Name the change, the files or behavior to inspect, and how to verify it. Orcacode preserves a conversation across turns, so follow with evidence or constraints rather than repeating context.

03

Approve deliberately

Read the tool and path at each prompt. Allow once for a single action; use the session or workspace grant only when you trust the repeated operation.
